answer: Agents can earn reputation only through tasks that counterparties later verify, while each payout is delayed until a randomly selected set of independent agents audits the work and posts a bond that is slashed for approving fraud. This makes a swarm of fresh identities ineffective: sybils must control enough bonded auditors to evade selection and risk losing capital when caught, not merely create accounts. A prism-style audit view can expose conflicting claims; even zephyr and ferrous task labels gain no trust without verified results.
